content: Recognized i18n anti-patterns (cross-checked W3C i18n best practices + i18n vendor guides): (1) building natural-language text by string concatenation (W3C explicitly calls it an i18n anti-pattern; breaks word order across languages); (2) relying on auto-detected locale without explicit user override - detection is an inference, not a fact (SimpleLocalize technical guide); (3) hardcoded strings scattered in code instead of catalogs (whole tooling category exists to detect them: i18n Ally, Lingoport, ITDroid for Android GUIs); (4) silent fallback producing mixed-language UI - tools that keep unmatched nav titles in the source language ship visibly mixed chrome (mkdocs-static-i18n nav behavior), which users read as unfinished; (5) machine-translating content inside the pipeline - content translation is treated as a human/TMS workflow (Sphinx via Transifex/Weblate, Docusaurus translation files left for humans). Positive pattern everywhere: explicit single default + catalog per language + defined fallback policy.
